articles.title: SJAA at Lick Observatory May 2016
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) hosted a special tour event at Lick Observatory on May 13, 2016, for 40 members and supporters. Attendees enjoyed presentations by Dr. Elinor Gates and Tanja Bode, a unique 'Ride the Dome' experience with the Shane telescope, and observing celestial objects like the M3 globular cluster and Jupiter through the historic 36" Great Refractor. The event successfully raised $2,000 to support Lick Observatory.

articles.title: Curiosity's 4th Anniversary on Mars
articles.summary: This article commemorates the Curiosity rover's fourth anniversary on Mars, highlighting its ongoing mission to collect samples, drill rocks like "Marimba," and ascend Mount Sharp to study ancient geological evidence of environmental evolution. It details the rover's past discovery of a freshwater lake at "Yellowknife Bay," indicating a once-habitable environment, and announces a new 'Mars Rover' social media game for public engagement related to future exploration technologies.

articles.title: A Hubble Sky Full of Stars
articles.summary: The Hubble Space Telescope captured a dazzling image of NGC 4833, a globular cluster located 22,000 light-years away in the constellation Musca. This tightly packed collection of ancient stars is one of over 150 such clusters in the Milky Way, providing astronomers valuable insights into the formation, evolution, and age of our galaxy.

articles.title: Five Years Post-Launch, Juno Is at a Turning Point
articles.summary: Five years post-launch, NASA's Juno spacecraft has reached a turning point after arriving at Jupiter, having completed its first apojove on July 31. It is currently in one of two long capture orbits, preparing for its science mission, with all instruments set to collect data during its first close pass over Jupiter on August 27. This pass will serve as a trial run before Juno shortens its orbit to 14 days and fully begins its mission to study Jupiter's deep structure, atmosphere, and magnetic environment.

articles.title: The Autumn Sky
articles.summary: This article outlines celestial events and observing opportunities for the autumn of 2016 (September-December), detailing the visibility and significant conjunctions for major planets like Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune. It also provides peak dates for meteor showers including the Orionids, Leonids, Geminids, and Ursids, alongside guidance on identifying constellations and news about an SJAA 'half' Messier marathon event.

articles.title: Pinnacles DSSH June 4, 2016
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association's (SJAA) Summer Deep Sky Scavenger Hunt at Pinnacles West Side on June 4, 2016, proved to be an exceptional observing event despite initial concerns about wildfire smoke. Organized by Ed Wong, participants enjoyed remarkably clear skies (SQM 21.69), successfully identifying numerous challenging deep-sky objects like Omega Centauri and Centaurus A. The event fostered significant camaraderie and skill development among club members, receiving widespread praise for its organization and excellent viewing conditions.

articles.title: SJAA Member Observation Posts
articles.summary: This article compiles several amateur astronomy observation reports from SJAA members in mid-2016, detailing various experiences from backyard planetary viewing to dark-sky deep-sky observing at remote sites. Members share insights on overcoming challenges like light pollution and poor seeing, utilizing different telescope equipment, and providing detailed descriptions of celestial objects ranging from planets and carbon stars to nebulae and star clusters. The reports also include reviews of observing locations and tips for visual astronomy and basic astrophotography.

articles.title: Cave Nebula
articles.summary: This document features two distinct astrophotography reports. Mark Striebeck details his deep-sky imaging of the Cave Nebula from Orange Spring Ranch, California, using specialized telescopes and cameras over 5.4 hours. Separately, Gary Chock describes capturing a rich-field Milky Way shot above the 'Mexican Mine Cabins' from the Ancient Bristlecone Pine Forest using a DSLR and a portable tracker.

articles.title: Eastern Veil - NGC 6995
articles.summary: Manoj Koushik presents an astrophotograph of the Eastern Veil Nebula (NGC 6995), captured from his new backyard 'Tapas Observatory' in San Jose, CA. The image is a culmination of 44 hours of integration over multiple nights in July 2016, detailing the specific telescope, camera, mount, filters, and processing software used. This project marks his return to astrophotography after a period of absence.

articles.title: Kid Spot
articles.summary: This 'Kid Spot' section offers an engaging blend of astronomy-related content, featuring space-themed jokes, a quiz on NASA's planetary missions, and a collection of 'Did You Know?' facts. Covering diverse topics from solar system features to stellar magnitudes and galaxy clusters, it provides educational and entertaining insights, likely aimed at a broad audience including younger readers. The content was published as part of the SJAA Ephemeris in September 2016.

articles.title: Board Meeting Excerpts
articles.summary: These board meeting excerpts from May, June, and July 2016 detail the San Jose Astronomical Association's administrative and operational discussions. Key topics included the transition to Google for Non Profits, organization of storage facilities, approval of the 2017 events calendar, and upgrades to club equipment like the Lunt Solar Scope and imaging camera. The board also addressed online security, a new lost and found policy, and community relations regarding observing spaces.

articles.title: SJAA Library!
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) provides a variety of resources and programs for its members and the community, including a library of astronomy books and DVDs. They offer practical support like free telescope repair sessions and an equipment loaner program, alongside educational initiatives such as solar observing, beginner-focused 'Quick STARt' and 'Intro to the Night Sky' sessions, and specialized astrophotography groups and workshops.
